display.purpose: The one oversized gothic line per page — hero headline and every PageHead title (narrowed to clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.5rem), capped at 18ch).

headline.purpose: Section heads, always capped at 16ch–20ch so they break like a sign rather than a paragraph.

title.purpose: Vehicle names and sub-section heads inside a band.

lede.purpose: The single paragraph under a heading. Auto-switches to ink-dim on concrete and signal-dim on enamel.

body.purpose: Running text at a 68ch measure; 1.7 line-height in legal prose.

label.purpose: Mono uppercase field labels, footer column heads, figure captions, blade keys. Always tracked 0.14em–0.20em.

coordinate.purpose: The mono azure line above a heading, with a trailing 1px rule. Must carry real information — a grid coordinate, a section index, a destination.

gothic.purpose: The sign-lettering modifier: uppercase at +0.02em on wordmark, service names, vehicle names, capacity labels.

fonts.name: Overpass Variable
fonts.rationale: Descends from Highway Gothic (the FHWA road-sign series). This is not a reference to signage lettering; it is the signage lettering.

fonts.name: Overpass Mono Variable
fonts.rationale: The monospaced sibling of the same family. Carries only what is measured or indexed.

shadows.name: press-rest

shadows.name: press-hover

shadows.name: press-active
shadows.purpose: Paired with translateY(1px) as the action is pressed home.

shadows.name: ghost-ring
shadows.purpose: The outlined action on enamel; goes to 0.75 opacity on hover. Inset so it never reads as cast.

shadows.name: focus-ring-input

shadows.name: focus-ring-global

motion.name: ease-out

motion.name: duration-link

narrative.overview:
This is Chicago's street-blade signage program rebuilt as a booking site. Every surface is a fabricated object: a porcelain enamel plate in deep green, faced with the logo chevron, lettered in Highway Gothic caps, punched with near-square corners, and marked in high-visibility amber only where something must be acted on. The system is built from six primitives — .field, .blade, .plate, .action, .coordinate, .control — and a page is assembled by alternating enamel bands against a concrete ground, not by stacking cards.

The density is civic rather than editorial: generous vertical bands (clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem)) around content that is itself tightly set, with headline tracking pulled in hard (-0.03em to -0.05em) and label tracking pushed out hard (0.10em to 0.20em). Nothing floats. Nothing glows. The one place the system moves mechanically is the destination blade on the quote and reservation forms, which rolls its vehicle line the way a coach's destination blind rolls.

The category anti-references are explicit and were refused by construction, not by taste: no stock highway photograph, no vehicle beauty shot, no translucent quote bar floating over a hero image. The build ships zero photographic assets. Proof is carried by numerals — two real capacities, 57 and 13, set at route-number scale — and by drawn geometry (the SeatPlan seating diagrams, the authored 24x24 icon set).
keyCharacteristics: Two color grounds — enamel green and concrete — and every component works on both
3px corners on every UI surface; a fabricated sign plate, not a web card
Amber exclusively for action, state and safety marking, held under a few percent of any viewport
Highway Gothic lineage: Overpass Variable, descended from the FHWA road-sign series
One elevation signal per surface — hairline or marked top edge, never both, never a shadow
Drawn proof over photographed proof: numerals, seat plans, authored icons

rules.name: The Amber-For-Action Rule
rules.body: Amber marks what a person must act on or attend to: actions, focus, the current location in nav, the system's own recommendation output, required-field marks, unresolved placeholders, and the hard top edge of a terminal band. It is held under a few percent of any viewport. Painting amber on a heading, a decorative rule, or a background field breaks the world.

rules.name: The Two-Grounds Rule
rules.body: Enamel and concrete are both first-class grounds. A component ships one base treatment plus a .field descendant override (.field .plate, .field .lede, :global(.field) .plan), never two parallel variants. Any new component must be checked on both grounds before it is done.

rules.name: The Azure Reserve Rule
rules.body: Azure appears only on mono type that names a coordinate, a key, or a measurement. It is never a fill, never a border, never running prose.

rules.name: The One-Motif Rule
rules.body: One motif, two registers. --enamel-pattern is the logo's sheared bar broken into a run of dashes at eight lengths over three uneven rows (96x60 tile, white fill at 0.05), on every enamel surface: the masthead, .field, .blade, .method--primary. --concrete-pattern is the owner's artwork at a much larger stride on the body. Neither crosses to the other ground and no surface carries both. The hero is the one concrete band held clean of the pattern — it paints --paper itself rather than letting the body's ground through, because a repeating pattern showing through a dissolving photo edge reads as dirt on the lens.

rules.name: The Masked-Ground Rule
rules.body: The hero photograph is never darkened, tinted, scrimmed, or panelled to carry type. It covers the whole band and is masked back into the ground: the band paints flat --paper and the photograph's alpha ramps from a few percent under the copy to fully opaque at the cab, so contrast is a fact about --paper rather than a bet on a photograph. Four steps, --ramp-1 5% to --ramp-4 48%, built with color-mix(in srgb, currentColor N%, transparent) — only a mask stop's alpha is read, so currentColor means fully opaque and no colour literal enters the ramp. Vertical below 64rem where the copy fills the box; horizontal above it, closing one step further at 80rem. A second single-layer mask on the wrapper dissolves the last sixth downward, rather than mask-composite, which fails open if a browser misses it. Every stop is set by sampling the rendered band with the copy hidden and reading the worst pixel under each line, not by eye. Consequences: nothing translucent stands on it (the phone button became an opaque paper-lift fill with a full-strength enamel ring; the hours divider went from --paper-line to currentColor at 0.4), and the hero shares its ground with the quote form with no border between them.

rules.name: The Highway Gothic Rule
rules.body: Overpass is the only voice. Its descent from the FHWA series is the reason it is here, so a second display face — a serif, a geometric, a condensed — would put a different road on the same sign. There is no second family beyond the mono sibling.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono carries only what is measured or indexed: coordinates, keys, counts, capacities, captions, timestamps, service designations. It never carries running prose and never sets a heading.

rules.name: The Tracking-Follows-Case Rule
rules.body: Uppercase always carries positive tracking (+0.02em on gothic display caps, 0.10em-0.20em on mono labels). Mixed-case display and headline always carry negative tracking (-0.02em to -0.05em). There is no uppercase run at neutral tracking anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The Coordinate-Carries-Information Rule
rules.body: The .coordinate line above a heading is a grid coordinate on a blade, not a marketing eyebrow. It must name a real location, a real section index, or a real destination. It must never restate the heading beneath it in softer words, and it must never be added purely to give a heading a hat. Its trailing rule is what makes it read as a sign's coordinate bar rather than a kicker.

rules.name: The One-Signal Rule
rules.body: A surface gets exactly one elevation signal. A .plate has a hairline border or a 3px marked top edge — never both, and never either plus a shadow.

rules.name: The Shadow-Is-Press Rule
rules.body: box-shadow belongs to the pressable and to focus. Plates, blades, the masthead, the mobile nav drawer, testimonial cards, and capacity plates all cast nothing.

rules.name: The Fabricated-Corner Rule
rules.body: 3px, everywhere, via var(--radius). Never 8px, 12px, or 16px. If a surface needs to feel softer, it needs a different ground, not a different corner.

rules.name: The Square-Plate Rule
rules.body: Radius and a marked top edge are mutually exclusive. A plate carrying border-top: 3px solid takes border-radius: 0. A plate carrying a full 1px border takes var(--radius).

rules.name: The Drawn-Proof Rule
rules.body: Evidence is drawn or set in type, never photographed. Capacity is a numeral at display scale, a layout is an SVG plan, an amenity is an authored icon. The build ships no photographic assets and no illustration library.

rules.name: The Mechanical-Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion depicts a mechanism. Arrows translate along their axis (4-5px on hover), list rows grow their inside gutter (padding-inline, 240ms) so the row appears to slide toward you, and the destination blade rolls. Durations are 160ms for input state, 180ms for actions, 200ms for links and hovers, 240ms for row expansion, and 420ms for the roll — all on --ease-out. Nothing fades in on scroll and nothing bounces. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses all animation and transition to 0.01ms globally.

dos: Do compose new surfaces from the six primitives — .field, .blade, .plate, .action, .coordinate, .control — before writing new component CSS.
Do open every interior page with a PageHead enamel band carrying a real coordinate line, a display title capped at 18ch, and an optional lede at 52ch.
Do alternate enamel and concrete bands down a page; a ground change is the section separator, not a border.
Do check every new component on both grounds and add a .field descendant override rather than a second class.
Do use var(--radius) (3px) for every UI corner, and drop to border-radius: 0 the moment a plate takes a 3px marked top edge.
Do set measured values — coordinates, counts, capacities, timings, captions — in Overpass Mono with .mono for tabular numerals.
Do draw new icons into Icon.astro's set at 24x24, stroke 2, square caps, miter joins, currentColor.
Do mark unresolved content with Placeholder.astro so it is impossible to mistake for shipped content.
donts: Don't paint amber on anything that is not an action, a focus or current state, a required mark, a system recommendation, or an unresolved item. It stays under a few percent of any viewport; that restraint is what keeps this civic rather than municipal-works.
Don't use any radius other than 3px on a UI surface, and don't combine a radius with a marked top edge.
Don't put a box-shadow on a plate, a blade, the masthead, or a card. Only .action casts, and only as a press affordance.

Don't cross the two patterns: --enamel-pattern never touches a concrete surface, --concrete-pattern never touches enamel, and no surface carries both. Don't raise either above the opacity it ships at.
Don't introduce a second display family, a glyph or emoji icon, or a system display face. Overpass and Overpass Mono are the whole voice.
Don't ship a stock highway photograph, a vehicle beauty shot, or a translucent quote bar floating over a hero image — the three things this world was built to refuse.
Don't write a kicker above a heading. The .coordinate line is the only line permitted there and it must carry real information; a line that restates the heading in softer words is not a coordinate.

Don't reference a spacing step outside the defined ramp (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32). Every step in that list is a real token in global.css; anything else resolves to nothing and is silently dropped at computed-value time.
Don't let a sticky element cover the thing it is confirming — the destination blade goes static below 46rem for exactly this reason.

brandMark.description: Horizontal lockup: three-chevron mark with a navy-to-green gradient beside the name set in three lines of navy.
brandMark.note: Sampled from the file. Documentation of the mark, not page colours — nothing on the site is painted with them.
brandMark.placement: Never on a dark field directly: navy measures 1.35:1 on --enamel. Sits on a --signal plate at --radius. Heights: 3rem masthead, 2.5rem below 30rem, 3.5rem footer.
brandMark.favicon: public/favicon.svg — the mark cropped from this same file via an SVG viewBox, not a substitute glyph.
